## Does the DR-learner close the gap on the causal forest with more signal?

In the main correlated binary study (`../`, ρ = 0.5) the DR-learners lose to
the causal forest, and SD(τ)/SD(noise) is at most 0.2 in scenarios 1–4
(`results_processing/thesis_figures/rel_eff_snr.R`). The Bernoulli noise is
about 0.46 whatever the DGM, so SNR can only rise through SD(τ). This check
moves away from the baseline (n = 500, HTE ×1) one factor at a time: a larger
HTE (`hte_mult` scales b3, b4, b34, b45, so more signal at n = 500) and a
larger n (more data at the baseline signal). 100 runs per cell. bW is
calibrated at n = 500 in every cell, so the ATE is −0.118 throughout, and the
treated risk is clamped into [0.01, 0.99] with the truth clamped to match.
Full design in `README.md`.

The n = 500 cells of a run share W and X across scenarios and multipliers, so
the `hte_mult` comparison is paired. The n cells are not. Scenario 1 has no
HTE, so it is on the n axis only.

```{r data}
res_path <- if (nzchar(params$res_path)) {
  params$res_path
} else {
  file.path(dirname(here()), "results", "correlated", "binary_snr")
}
figdir <- if (nzchar(params$fig_dir)) {
  params$fig_dir
} else {
  file.path(dirname(here()), "results", "all_figures", "correlated_binary_snr")
}
dir.create(figdir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

population <- readRDS(file.path(res_path, "bin_snr_population.RDS"))
metrics <- readRDS(file.path(res_path, "bin_snr_metrics.RDS"))
ratios <- readRDS(file.path(res_path, "bin_snr_ratios.RDS"))

CF_ARM <- "causal_forest"
# display order
ARMS <- c("causal_forest", "dr_random_forest", "dr_semi_oracle", "dr_oracle",
          "t_random_forest")
ARM_LABELS <- MODEL_LABELS[ARMS]
# named, so a figure without the CF keeps the other arms' colours
ARM_COLOURS <- setNames(
  as.character(paletteer::paletteer_d("rcartocolor::Safe")[seq_along(ARMS)]),
  ARM_LABELS
)

# as bin_corr_results.qmd, so the reports read side by side
SCENARIO_LABELS <- c(
  `1` = "1: No HTE",
  `2` = "2: Continuous HTE",
  `3` = "3: Two vars + cts x cts",
  `4` = "4: Cosine HTE"
)

HTE_LEVELS <- c(1, 1.5, 2, 3)
N_LEVELS <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 4000)

# both factors go on one numeric x, hte_mult at 1-4 and n at 11-14, so a
# single facet_grid() can show them side by side with free x and one y per row.
# SNR differs by scenario, so it is written inside each panel, not on the axis
X_BREAKS <- c(seq_along(HTE_LEVELS), 10 + seq_along(N_LEVELS))
X_LABELS <- c(paste0("×", HTE_LEVELS), format(N_LEVELS, big.mark = ","))
PANEL_LABELS <- c(
  hte = "More signal: HTE multiplier at n = 500",
  n = "More data: n at HTE ×1"
)
Z <- qnorm(0.975)

# each cell's population SNR, for the panel annotations. The n cells sit at
# their scenario's x1 SNR
snr_cells <- bind_rows(
  population %>% mutate(n = 500),
  population %>% filter(hte_mult == 1) %>% tidyr::crossing(n = N_LEVELS[-1])
)
```

```{r helpers}
#' Put each row on the panel(s) it belongs to. The baseline (n = 500,
#' hte_mult 1) is in both
on_axes <- function(df) {
  bind_rows(
    df %>%
      filter(n == 500) %>%
      mutate(panel = "hte", pos = match(hte_mult, HTE_LEVELS)),
    df %>%
      filter(hte_mult == 1) %>%
      mutate(panel = "n", pos = 10 + match(n, N_LEVELS))
  ) %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(PANEL_LABELS[panel], levels = PANEL_LABELS),
           scenario = factor(SCENARIO_LABELS[as.character(scenario)],
                             levels = SCENARIO_LABELS))
}

#' The arm's label and dodged x
add_arm <- function(df, arms) {
  k <- length(arms)
  df %>%
    mutate(
      arm = factor(ARM_LABELS[model], levels = ARM_LABELS[arms]),
      x = pos + (match(model, arms) - (k + 1) / 2) * 0.7 / k
    )
}

#' Estimate +/- interval per arm and cell, the hte_mult and n panels side by
#' side, a row per scenario, each column's population SNR along the bottom
#'
#' @param est scenario, n, hte_mult, model, est, lo, hi
#' @param runs optional scenario, n, hte_mult, model, value: per-run points
#'   drawn faintly behind the estimates
#' @param yref a dashed reference line, NA for none
snr_plot <- function(est, ylab, title, runs = NULL, yref = NA, log_y = FALSE) {
  arms <- intersect(ARMS, unique(est$model))
  # scenario 1 has no HTE, so no SNR to print
  snr_lab <- snr_cells %>%
    filter(scenario %in% unique(est$scenario), scenario != 1) %>%
    on_axes() %>%
    mutate(label = sprintf("SNR %.2f", snr))
  est <- est %>% on_axes() %>% add_arm(arms)
  p <- ggplot(est, aes(x, est, colour = arm, group = arm))
  if (!is.na(yref)) {
    p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = yref, linetype = "dashed",
                        colour = "grey50")
  }
  if (!is.null(runs)) {
    set.seed(1)
    runs <- runs %>%
      on_axes() %>%
      add_arm(arms) %>%
      mutate(x = x + runif(n(), -0.3, 0.3) * 0.7 / length(arms))
    p <- p + geom_point(data = runs, aes(y = value), shape = 16, size = 0.4,
                        alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE)
  }
  p <- p +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    # 0 is -Inf once logged, so either way the text sits on the panel floor
    geom_text(data = snr_lab,
              aes(x = pos, y = if (log_y) 0 else -Inf, label = label),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.5, size = 2.5,
              colour = "grey40") +
    facet_grid(scenario ~ panel, scales = "free", space = "free_x") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = X_BREAKS, labels = X_LABELS,
                       expand = expansion(add = 0.4)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = ARM_COLOURS) +
    drf_theme() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
    labs(title = title, x = NULL, y = ylab, colour = "Arm")
  # extra room at the bottom so the SNR text clears the data
  y_expand <- expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.05))
  p + if (log_y) {
    scale_y_log10(expand = y_expand)
  } else {
    scale_y_continuous(expand = y_expand)
  }
}

#' Mean +/- 95% CI (mean +/- z x MCSE) of one metric, per arm and cell
metric_est <- function(df, col) {
  df %>%
    group_by(scenario, n, hte_mult, model) %>%
    summarise(
      est = mean(.data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE),
      mcse = sd(.data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(.data[[col]]))),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(is.finite(est)) %>%
    mutate(lo = est - Z * mcse, hi = est + Z * mcse)
}

#' Rejection rate at HTE_ALPHA of one test's p-value, with the binomial MCSE.
#' Runs with an NA p-value are left out
power_est <- function(df, col) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) %>%
    group_by(scenario, n, hte_mult, model) %>%
    summarise(runs = n(), est = mean(.data[[col]] < HTE_ALPHA),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(mcse = sqrt(est * (1 - est) / runs),
           lo = pmax(est - Z * mcse, 0), hi = pmin(est + Z * mcse, 1))
}

#' One tab per spec, written from a results="asis" chunk. A spec is a list of
#' tab, plot and optionally save (a file name in figdir)
plot_tabs <- function(specs) {
  cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (s in specs) {
    # knitr drops the newlines after a printed plot, so each cat() leads with
    # blank lines or the next heading glues onto the image
    cat("\n\n##", s$tab, "\n\n")
    print(s$plot)
    if (!is.null(s$save)) {
      ggsave(s$save, plot = s$plot, path = figdir, height = 24, width = 28,
             units = "cm")
    }
  }
  cat("\n\n:::\n\n")
}

cell_order <- function(df) arrange(df, scenario, desc(n == 500), n, hte_mult)
```

## Population truth

Per scenario and HTE multiplier, from the clamped truth over 10^6 ρ = 0.5
covariate draws (`bin_snr_metrics.R`). SNR is `rel_eff_snr.R`'s
SD(τ) / sqrt(E[p(1 − p)]). The ATE drifts a little from −0.118 only where the
treated risk is clamped.

```{r population}
population %>%
  mutate(scenario = SCENARIO_LABELS[as.character(scenario)],
         share_clamped = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * share_clamped)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("Scenario", "HTE ×", "bW", "ATE", "SD(τ)", "SD(noise)",
                      "SNR", "Treated risk clamped"))
```

## Results coverage

The expected count is 100 runs per cell and arm.

```{r coverage}
coverage <- metrics %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, hte_mult, model) %>%
  summarise(runs = n_distinct(run), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(model = factor(ARM_LABELS[model], levels = ARM_LABELS)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = runs, names_sort = TRUE) %>%
  cell_order()
kable(coverage, col.names = c("Scenario", "n", "HTE ×", names(coverage)[-(1:3)]))
```

```{r na-table}
na_table <- metrics %>%
  group_by(scenario, n, hte_mult, model) %>%
  summarise(runs_with_na = sum(n_na > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            total_na = sum(n_na, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(total_na > 0) %>%
  mutate(model = ARM_LABELS[model]) %>%
  cell_order()
if (nrow(na_table) > 0) {
  kable(na_table, col.names = c("Scenario", "n", "HTE ×", "Arm",
                                "Runs with an NA estimate", "Total NA estimates"))
} else {
  cat("No missing CATE estimates in any collected run.")
}
```

## RMSE ratio, arm / causal forest

This is the comparison the study exists for. Each faint point is one run's
RMSE of an arm divided by the same run's causal forest RMSE (`rel_eff_snr.R`'s
ratio). Below 1 (dashed), the arm did better. The larger point is the
geometric mean, exp(mean log ratio), with a 95% CI from the MCSE of the mean
log ratio. The y axis is on a log scale. Each column's population SNR is
printed along the bottom of its panel.

```{r ratio-plot, fig.height=11}
run_ratios <- metrics %>%
  filter(model != CF_ARM) %>%
  select(scenario, n, hte_mult, run, model, rmse) %>%
  inner_join(
    metrics %>%
      filter(model == CF_ARM) %>%
      select(scenario, n, hte_mult, run, rmse_cf = rmse),
    by = c("scenario", "n", "hte_mult", "run")
  ) %>%
  mutate(value = rmse / rmse_cf) %>%
  filter(is.finite(value), value > 0)

ratio_ci <- ratios %>%
  mutate(est = geo_mean,
         lo = exp(log(geo_mean) - Z * mcse_log),
         hi = exp(log(geo_mean) + Z * mcse_log))

p_ratio <- snr_plot(
  ratio_ci,
  ylab = "RMSE ratio, arm / causal forest",
  title = "Each arm against the causal forest",
  runs = run_ratios, yref = 1, log_y = TRUE
)
p_ratio
ggsave("bin_snr_ratio.png", plot = p_ratio, path = figdir, height = 24,
       width = 28, units = "cm")
```

### Against population SNR

The n = 500 cells of scenarios 2–4 only, with the geometric-mean ratio
against the cell's population SNR: `rel_eff_snr.R`'s view, carried past the
main study's SNR ceiling of about 0.2.

```{r ratio-vs-snr, fig.height=5}
p_ratio_snr <- ratio_ci %>%
  filter(n == 500, scenario != 1) %>%
  mutate(arm = factor(ARM_LABELS[model], levels = ARM_LABELS),
         scenario = factor(SCENARIO_LABELS[as.character(scenario)],
                           levels = SCENARIO_LABELS)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(snr, est, colour = arm, group = arm)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = ARM_COLOURS) +
  drf_theme() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "RMSE ratio to the causal forest against population SNR, n = 500",
       x = "Population SNR, SD(τ) / SD(noise)",
       y = "RMSE ratio, arm / causal forest", colour = "Arm")
p_ratio_snr
ggsave("bin_snr_ratio_vs_snr.png", plot = p_ratio_snr, path = figdir,
       height = 12, width = 28, units = "cm")
```

```{r ratio-table}
ratio_ci %>%
  mutate(
    scenario = SCENARIO_LABELS[as.character(scenario)],
    model = ARM_LABELS[model],
    median_iqr = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median, q25, q75),
    geo_ci = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", geo_mean, lo, hi)
  ) %>%
  select(model, scenario, n, hte_mult, snr, runs, median_iqr, geo_ci,
         prop_better) %>%
  arrange(factor(model, levels = ARM_LABELS), scenario, desc(n == 500), n,
          hte_mult) %>%
  kable(digits = 2,
        col.names = c("Arm", "Scenario", "n", "HTE ×", "SNR", "Runs",
                      "Median [IQR]", "Geometric mean (95% CI)",
                      "Share of runs arm better"))
```

## Absolute performance

Mean ± 95% CI (1.96 × MCSE) for every arm, the causal forest included. τ
itself grows with the HTE multiplier, so RMSE and bias are not comparable
across the left panel's columns. The ratio above is the like-for-like
comparison. Correlation is scale-free; it is set to 0 in scenario 1, which is
left out of that tab.

```{r abs-plots, results="asis", fig.height=10}
abs_specs <- list(
  list(tab = "RMSE", col = "rmse", ylab = "Mean RMSE",
       title = "RMSE of the CATE estimates", save = "bin_snr_rmse.png"),
  list(tab = "Bias", col = "bias", ylab = "Mean bias", yref = 0,
       title = "Bias in the CATE estimates (estimate − truth)"),
  list(tab = "Correlation", col = "corr", ylab = "Mean correlation",
       title = "Correlation with the true CATE", hte_only = TRUE),
  list(tab = "Sign accuracy", col = "sign_acc", ylab = "Mean sign accuracy",
       title = "Share of units with the sign of τ right")
)
plot_tabs(lapply(abs_specs, function(s) {
  df <- if (isTRUE(s$hte_only)) filter(metrics, scenario != 1) else metrics
  list(
    tab = s$tab, save = s$save,
    plot = snr_plot(metric_est(df, s$col), ylab = s$ylab,
                    title = s$title, yref = if (is.null(s$yref)) NA else s$yref)
  )
}))
```

## HTE test power

The share of runs each test rejects at α = `r HTE_ALPHA`, ± 95% CI from the
binomial MCSE. In scenario 1 there is no HTE, so its row is the type I error
(dashed line at α). Runs with an NA p-value are left out: the PO independence
test is not run for the causal forest.

```{r power-plots, results="asis", fig.height=10}
power_specs <- list(
  list(tab = "BLP (two-sided)", col = "BLP_p", save = "bin_snr_power_blp.png"),
  list(tab = "BLP (one-sided)", col = "BLP_p_os"),
  list(tab = "Independence, CATE", col = "indep_cate"),
  list(tab = "Independence, PO", col = "indep_po")
)
plot_tabs(lapply(power_specs, function(s) {
  list(
    tab = s$tab, save = s$save,
    plot = snr_plot(power_est(metrics, s$col), ylab = "Rejection rate",
                    title = paste("Power of the", s$tab, "test"),
                    yref = HTE_ALPHA)
  )
}))
```

## DR-RandomForest against the DR-semi-oracle

Paired per-run differences, DR-RandomForest minus DR-semi-oracle (true
propensity 0.5), averaged with MCSE = sd(diff) / √pairs. A positive RMSE
difference means estimating the propensity costs accuracy. Unlike
competing_risk/snr's semi-oracle twins, `dr_semi_oracle` refits its own
outcome forests, so the gap is the propensity plus forest Monte Carlo noise
(`README.md`, Arms).

```{r semi-plots, results="asis", fig.height=10}
paired_semi <- metrics %>%
  filter(model %in% c("dr_random_forest", "dr_semi_oracle")) %>%
  select(scenario, n, hte_mult, run, model, rmse, corr) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = c(rmse, corr)) %>%
  mutate(model = "dr_random_forest",
         rmse = rmse_dr_random_forest - rmse_dr_semi_oracle,
         corr = corr_dr_random_forest - corr_dr_semi_oracle)

plot_tabs(list(
  list(tab = "RMSE", save = "bin_snr_semi_rmse.png",
       plot = snr_plot(metric_est(paired_semi, "rmse"),
                       ylab = "RMSE difference",
                       title = "Paired difference in RMSE, estimated − true propensity",
                       yref = 0)),
  list(tab = "Correlation",
       plot = snr_plot(metric_est(filter(paired_semi, scenario != 1), "corr"),
                       ylab = "Correlation difference",
                       title = "Paired difference in correlation, estimated − true propensity",
                       yref = 0))
))
```
